title: Standard Operating Procedure: Slicing an Apple

steps.step: Prepare the workspace and inspect the apple
steps.purpose: Ensure the equipment and the apple itself are ready before cutting begins.

tasks.task: Inspect the apple for surface defects
actions: Examine the apple's skin for blemishes such as discoloration or frost burn.
Judge whether the blemish is only cosmetic before proceeding.

decision_points.condition: A blemish such as frost burn is found on the skin
decision_points.response: Judge that it will not affect the flesh and continue cutting without changing technique.

actions: Touch the near corner of the board to confirm it is clear and stable before beginning.
Pick up a knife intended for the cut.
Confirm it is the correct knife for the task before proceeding.

decision_points.condition: The knife picked up is not the one intended for the task
decision_points.response: Set it aside and pick up the correct knife instead.

steps.step: Cut a section from the apple
steps.purpose: Separate a workable section of flesh from the core piece so it can be sliced.
steps.repeats: Repeat for each section until the apple is fully used

tasks.task: Position the apple or remaining piece for cutting
actions: Hold the apple, or the remaining piece after earlier cuts, upright against the board with the non-dominant hand.
Bring the knife blade into position against the piece with the dominant hand, aligning the cut beside the core.
Draw the knife down through the piece in a continuous stroke, separating a section from the core piece, or from the remaining piece on later cuts.
Lift the knife and the freed section clear of the board.

decision_points.condition: The remaining piece is easier to cut from a different side than the previous cut
decision_points.response: Reposition the piece and cut the next section from that side instead.

actions: On the first cut only, set the core piece down at a corner of the board, clear of the working area.
Retain the freed section in hand for slicing.

steps.purpose: Reduce each section into individual slices that make up the finished product.
steps.repeats: Repeat for each slice until the section is fully used, then repeat this step for each section produced from the apple

tasks.task: Trim uneven edges from the section
actions: If the section has an uneven or skin-covered edge, position that edge under the knife blade.
Draw the knife down to trim away the scrap, reposition the piece, and repeat until the edge is even.
Set the trimmed scrap aside, away from the slices.
Hold the section upright between the fingers of the non-dominant hand.
Draw the knife down through the section with the dominant hand, cutting a slice free.
Reposition or rotate the section after each cut to steady the shrinking piece.
Continue cutting slices until the section is fully used.

decision_points.condition: A cut slice is judged too thin
decision_points.response: Note the result but continue cutting slices using the same technique.

actions: Judge the quality of the slices produced.
If a leftover piece is too small or irregular to yield a further usable slice, set it aside as scrap rather than attempting another cut.

decision_points.condition: The leftover piece is too small or irregular to yield a usable slice
decision_points.response: Set it aside as scrap instead of cutting further.

steps.purpose: Group the finished slices for easy handling and mark the apple as complete.

actions: Use the flat of the knife blade or the hand to press and sweep the slices together.
Consolidate them into a single compact cluster at a corner of the board.
Set the knife down on the counter or board, clear of the slices.
Confirm the apple is fully sliced, with the core piece and any scrap separated from the finished slices.

synthesis_notes: Merged Georgia's board-check and knife-selection tasks with Tori's apple-inspection step into a single 'Prepare the workspace and inspect the apple' step, since all three are one-off checks performed before the main cutting sequence begins.

Collapsed Tori's repeated 'cut and slice the second/third/final section' steps into one looping 'Cut a section from the apple' step and one looping 'Cut the section into slices' step, since they represent the same two tasks repeated across multiple sections of the same apple.

Folded Alice's one-off 'Evaluate cut quality' action and Tori's judgment that a leftover piece was too small to slice into a single 'Evaluate and clear remaining scrap' task within the slicing step, since both are end-of-section quality judgments rather than distinct phases.

Demoted Georgia's scrap-trimming actions (evening out the section's edge before cutting slices) from an implied separate step into a 'Trim uneven edges from the section' task nested inside the slicing step, since it is a preparatory habit performed within slicing, not its own phase.

Merged Alice's 'Clear and arrange the slices' step, Georgia's 'Consolidate the slices' task, and Tori's 'Conclude the session' step into one final 'Consolidate the slices and finish' step, since all three describe the same closing actions of gathering slices, setting down the knife, and confirming completion.
Standardized differing terms across runs (e.g. 'cheek', 'chunk', 'wedge', 'sliver', 'offcut') to the canonical nouns 'section', 'slice', and 'scrap' throughout the procedure for consistency.

Treated Georgia's brief board touch and mis-picked knife as sub-tasks within the single workspace-preparation step rather than standalone steps, since they were quick asides before the main cutting work, not separate phases of the procedure.
